ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
While exploring outer space, Darth Vader comes upon a purely reflective spherical planet with radius $R_{p}=$ $40,000 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $M_{p}=8.128 \times 10^{24} \mathrm{~kg}$. Around the planet is a strange moon of orbital radius $R_{s}=$ $6,400,000 \mathrm{~m}\left(R_{s} \gg R_{p}\right)$ and mass $M_{s}=9.346 \times 10^{19} \mathrm{~kg}\left(M_{s} \ll M_{p}\right)$. The moon can be modelled as a blackbody and absorbs light perfectly. Darth Vader is in the same plane that the planet orbits in. Startled, Darth Vader shoots a laser with constant intensity and power $P_{0}=2 \times 10^{32} \mathrm{~W}$ at the reflective planet and hits the planet a distance of $\frac{R_{p}}{2}$ away from the line from him to the center of the planet. Upon hitting the reflective planet, the light from the laser is plane polarized. The angle of the planet's polarizer is always the same as the angle of reflection. After reflectance, the laser lands a direct hit on the insulator planet. Darth Vader locks the laser in on the planet until it moves right in front of him, when he turns the laser off. Determine the energy absorbed by the satellite. Assume the reflective planet remains stationary and that the reflective planet is a perfect polarizer of light.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, on the left side there is a black dot representing Darth Vader/the laser source, and a horizontal laser is emitted from left to right toward a large gray reflecting sphere. The laser hits near the left-side surface of the sphere, and the hit point is offset relative to the horizontal dashed line passing through the center of the sphere; the offset distance marked in the figure is Rp/2. Outside the sphere there is a dashed circular orbit, representing the satellite orbit; a smaller dark gray satellite is located on the upper-left orbit. From the hit point on the reflecting sphere there is a reflected ray slanting toward the upper left, just hitting the satellite. Reasoning: According to the specified method, use the orbital polar angle φ of the satellite's revolution as the integration variable. The incident light is horizontal, the vertical offset of the hit point from the center line is Rp/2, and the radius of the reflecting sphere is Rp, so the initial incident/reflection angle satisfies sin θ_i = (Rp/2)/Rp = 1/2, therefore θ_i = π/6. For reflection of horizontal incident light on a spherical mirror, the orbital polar angle of the satellite hit after reflection satisfies φ = π - 2θ. Initially θ_i = π/6, so φ_i = π - 2(π/6) = 2π/3. Darth Vader is on the left side, and when the satellite moves to be directly facing Darth Vader it is in the left-side direction, therefore φ_f = π. Since Mp is much greater than Ms, take the satellite angular velocity as the circular-orbit angular velocity ω = sqrt(G Mp / Rs^3). Substituting G = 6.674×10^-11 SI, Mp = 8.128×10^24 kg, Rs = 6.4×10^6 m, gives ω = sqrt((6.674×10^-11)(8.128×10^24)/(6.4×10^6)^3) ≈ 1.44×10^-3 s^-1. The reflecting sphere is a perfect polarizer, and the polarizer angle equals the reflection angle; according to Malus' law, the power absorbed by the satellite after reflection is P(φ) = P0 cos^2 θ = P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2]. The satellite is a blackbody, and when directly hit it completely absorbs this power. Thus the total absorbed energy is E = ∫_{φ_i}^{φ_f} P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ / ω = (P0/ω) ∫_{2π/3}^{π} cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ. The value of this integral is π/6 + sqrt(3)/4, so E = (P0/ω)(π/6 + sqrt(3)/4). Substituting P0 = 2×10^32 W and ω ≈ 1.44×10^-3 s^-1, gives E ≈ 1.33×10^35 J.

method.method_draft: Use the orbital angle as the integration variable. From the image, read the initial geometry: a horizontal laser from the left strikes the reflective planet off-center by the marked distance Rp/2 and reflects upward-left to the moon on the dashed circular orbit. From the text, take Rp, Mp, Rs, P0, the perfect absorption by the moon, and the statement that the polarizer angle equals the reflection angle. The offset gives the initial incidence/reflection angle θ_i by sin θ_i = (Rp/2)/Rp = 1/2, so θ_i = π/6. For a horizontal incoming ray reflecting from the spherical mirror, the outgoing orbital polar angle of the moon is φ = π - 2θ, so initially φ_i = 2π/3 and when the moon is directly in front of Darth Vader it is at φ_f = π. The moon moves with constant angular speed ω = sqrt(GMp/Rs^3). Use Malus’ law for the reflected polarized beam, P(φ) = P0 cos^2 θ = P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2]. Then integrate the absorbed energy over the orbital arc: E = ∫_{φ_i}^{φ_f} P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ/ω = (P0/ω)(π/6 + sqrt(3)/4), which evaluates to about 1.33 × 10^35 J.

图像描述：图中左侧有一个黑点表示 Darth Vader/激光来源，一条水平激光从左向右射向灰色的大反射球体。激光击中球体左侧表面附近，击中点相对于通过球心的水平虚线偏离，图中标注偏离距离为 Rp/2。球体外有一条虚线圆轨道，表示卫星轨道；一个较小的深灰色卫星位于左上方轨道上。从反射球体击中点有一条反射光线斜向左上方，正好打到卫星。

推理：按指定方法，用卫星绕行的轨道极角 φ 作为积分变量。入射光是水平的，击中点距中心线的垂直偏移为 Rp/2，而反射球半径为 Rp，所以初始入射/反射角满足 sin θ_i = (Rp/2)/Rp = 1/2，因此 θ_i = π/6。对于水平入射光在球面镜上的反射，反射后击中卫星的轨道极角满足 φ = π - 2θ。初始时 θ_i = π/6，所以 φ_i = π - 2(π/6) = 2π/3。Darth Vader 在左侧，卫星运动到正对 Darth Vader 时位于左侧方向，因此 φ_f = π。

由于 Mp 远大于 Ms，卫星角速度取圆轨道角速度 ω = sqrt(G Mp / Rs^3)。代入 G = 6.674×10^-11 SI, Mp = 8.128×10^24 kg, Rs = 6.4×10^6 m，得到 ω = sqrt((6.674×10^-11)(8.128×10^24)/(6.4×10^6)^3) ≈ 1.44×10^-3 s^-1。

反射球为完美偏振器，偏振器角度等于反射角，按 Malus 定律，反射后被卫星吸收的功率为 P(φ) = P0 cos^2 θ = P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2]。卫星为黑体，直接命中时完全吸收该功率。于是总吸收能量为 E = ∫_{φ_i}^{φ_f} P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ / ω = (P0/ω) ∫_{2π/3}^{π} cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ。该积分值为 π/6 + sqrt(3)/4，所以 E = (P0/ω)(π/6 + sqrt(3)/4)。代入 P0 = 2×10^32 W 和 ω ≈ 1.44×10^-3 s^-1，得到 E ≈ 1.33×10^35 J。

raw_record.original_question: While exploring outer space, Darth Vader comes upon a purely reflective spherical planet with radius $R_{p}=40{,}000\ \mathrm{m}$ and mass $M_{p}=8.128 \times 10^{24}\ \mathrm{kg}$. Around the planet is a strange moon of orbital radius $R_{s}=6{,}400{,}000\ \mathrm{m}\ (R_{s} \gg R_{p})$ and mass $M_{s}=9.346 \times 10^{19}\ \mathrm{kg}\ (M_{s} \ll M_{p})$. The moon can be modelled as a blackbody and absorbs light perfectly. Darth Vader is in the same plane that the planet orbits in. Startled, Darth Vader shoots a laser with constant intensity and power $P_{0}=2 \times 10^{32}\ \mathrm{W}$ at the reflective planet and hits the planet a distance of $\frac{R_{p}}{2}$ away from the line from him to the center of the planet. Upon hitting the reflective planet, the light from the laser is plane polarized. The angle of the planet's polarizer is always the same as the angle of reflection. After reflectance, the laser lands a direct hit on the insulator planet. Darth Vader locks the laser in on the planet until it moves right in front of him, when he turns the laser off. Determine the energy absorbed by the satellite. Assume the reflective planet remains stationary and that the reflective planet is a perfect polarizer of light.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, on the left side there is a black dot representing Darth Vader/the laser source, and a horizontal laser is emitted from left to right toward a large gray reflecting sphere. The laser hits near the left-side surface of the sphere, and the hit point is offset relative to the horizontal dashed line passing through the center of the sphere; the offset distance marked in the figure is Rp/2. Outside the sphere there is a dashed circular orbit, representing the satellite orbit; a smaller dark gray satellite is located on the upper-left orbit. From the hit point on the reflecting sphere there is a reflected ray slanting toward the upper left, just hitting the satellite.

Reasoning: According to the specified method, use the orbital polar angle φ of the satellite's revolution as the integration variable. The incident light is horizontal, the vertical offset of the hit point from the center line is Rp/2, and the radius of the reflecting sphere is Rp, so the initial incident/reflection angle satisfies sin θ_i = (Rp/2)/Rp = 1/2, therefore θ_i = π/6. For reflection of horizontal incident light on a spherical mirror, the orbital polar angle of the satellite hit after reflection satisfies φ = π - 2θ. Initially θ_i = π/6, so φ_i = π - 2(π/6) = 2π/3. Darth Vader is on the left side, and when the satellite moves to be directly facing Darth Vader it is in the left-side direction, therefore φ_f = π.

Since Mp is much greater than Ms, take the satellite angular velocity as the circular-orbit angular velocity ω = sqrt(G Mp / Rs^3). Substituting G = 6.674×10^-11 SI, Mp = 8.128×10^24 kg, Rs = 6.4×10^6 m, gives ω = sqrt((6.674×10^-11)(8.128×10^24)/(6.4×10^6)^3) ≈ 1.44×10^-3 s^-1.

The reflecting sphere is a perfect polarizer, and the polarizer angle equals the reflection angle; according to Malus' law, the power absorbed by the satellite after reflection is P(φ) = P0 cos^2 θ = P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2]. The satellite is a blackbody, and when directly hit it completely absorbs this power. Thus the total absorbed energy is E = ∫_{φ_i}^{φ_f} P0 cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ / ω = (P0/ω) ∫_{2π/3}^{π} cos^2[(π - φ)/2] dφ. The value of this integral is π/6 + sqrt(3)/4, so E = (P0/ω)(π/6 + sqrt(3)/4). Substituting P0 = 2×10^32 W and ω ≈ 1.44×10^-3 s^-1, gives E ≈ 1.33×10^35 J.
